5-Star Boutique Resort · Non Nuoc Beach · Da Nang

Naman Retreat Da Nang Review

RY
Ryan Yousefi
Da Nang Hotel Guide · Last updated March 2026 · ★★★★★ · From $200/night
DesignCouplesAdultsVo Trong Nghia

Naman Retreat is the Non Nuoc property that architects and design-industry people recommend to each other — a Vietnamese design statement that treats the resort as a piece of architecture first and a hotel second.

Naman was designed by Vo Trong Nghia Architects, the Vietnamese firm that has become one of Asia's most internationally recognised architecture practices. The result is a resort built from bamboo, concrete, and tropical greenery in a way that creates distinct spaces without ever feeling like a theme park interpretation of Vietnam.

The bamboo tunnel that leads from reception to the beach pool complex is the most photographed architectural element, but it's not a gimmick — it sets a spatial tone that the rest of the resort sustains. You spend a weekend at Naman and come away thinking about how the spaces worked rather than about the food or the thread count.

The comparison set is TIA Wellness for wellness-brand identity, and the Marriott or Hyatt for beach resort facilities. Naman is neither of those things — it occupies a space defined by design and atmosphere rather than spa programming or pool count. Whether that's the right product depends on what you want from a resort stay.

Location & Getting There

Truong Sa Street, Ngu Hanh Son District — Non Nuoc Beach, 13km from Da Nang city centre. Same coastal strip as the Hyatt and Marriott, slightly south. Airport is 20–22 minutes. Hoi An is 30–35 minutes. Marble Mountains are 12 minutes north.

The Non Nuoc beach position is the same strong one that the rest of the resort strip shares — wide beach, calm water compared to My Khe, maintained and lifeguarded. Beach access from Naman feels different than from most Non Nuoc resorts because the approach through the bamboo walkways and gardens creates a sense of arrival at the ocean rather than just exiting the pool area.

City dining requires the same Grab commitment as all Non Nuoc resorts. The resort is self-contained enough that most guests don't leave often. For guests who want a resort where staying put is the point, Naman's design makes that commitment feel like the right one.

The Rooms

Room categories from superior rooms through pool villas to beach villas. The architecture is the product here — every room type exists within a design framework that prioritises natural light, cross-ventilation, and the visual integration of the tropical landscape. Some rooms have direct views into bamboo garden spaces that feel genuinely private.

Pool villas are the category that defines Naman's identity: each with a private pool set within a bamboo and greenery enclosure, designed for total privacy without feeling claustrophobic. The quality of these spaces — how they handle light in the morning, how the bamboo filters the afternoon heat — is the result of a genuinely considered design process.

Standard rooms are 50–60sqm and designed with the same care as the villa categories. The materials throughout — polished concrete, bamboo, reclaimed timber — are consistent with the architectural brief and maintained to a high standard. Rates from $200–350/night for pool villas in shoulder season.

Pool, Beach & Facilities

The main pool complex runs through the centre of the resort in a long bamboo-framed corridor — the approach to the pool is part of the experience rather than just a path to reach it. The pool is well-proportioned and the design creates a sense of enclosure without blocking the tropical light.

Non Nuoc Beach direct access. Beach service is provided and the beach in front of Naman is maintained. The beach here is the same Non Nuoc quality as the rest of the strip — wide, relatively calm, good for swimming in most months.

Spa at Naman is a proper operation with a comprehensive treatment menu. The spa spaces are architecturally consistent with the rest of the property — bamboo and concrete pavilions that function as proper treatment spaces. Quality is at the upper end of the Non Nuoc tier.

No kids' club — Naman is pitched at couples and design-conscious travellers rather than families. The atmosphere reflects this. Families with young children will find the InterContinental-style 'wrong for families' description applies here too.

Food & Drink

Hay Hay restaurant is the signature dining venue and takes its food seriously — a Vietnamese-focused menu with local ingredients and a kitchen that treats dinner as part of the overall design experience rather than a convenience. The terrace setting in the bamboo gardens, with proper lighting at night, produces one of the more memorable dining environments in Da Nang.

Nest by Naman is the beach bar and casual dining option — good for lunch, cocktails at sunset, and the kind of light evening eating that suits a slow resort day. The beach position and the bamboo structure of the bar itself make it worth an hour regardless of what you're drinking.

Breakfast is served at Hay Hay and takes the same approach as the rest of the food operation: quality ingredients, properly executed. Vietnamese and international options. A slow breakfast at Naman — when the morning light comes through the bamboo and the staff aren't yet managing peak-service numbers — is one of the better resort mornings available in Da Nang.

The bamboo tunnel, the pool villas, the way the light moves through the resort in the morning — Naman treats design as the amenity. If that resonates, nothing else in Da Nang competes.

The Good Stuff

  • Architecture by Vo Trong Nghia — the most design-distinctive resort in Da Nang by significant margin
  • Pool villas set within bamboo garden enclosures — genuine privacy and spatial quality
  • Restaurant and bar settings are as considered as the rooms — design runs through the entire experience
  • Non Nuoc Beach access comparable to more expensive Marriott and Hyatt neighbours
  • Spa quality at the top end of the Non Nuoc tier

Watch Out For

  • No kids' club — wrong choice for families with young children
  • Pool villa rates premium — comparable to or above Marriott beach villa pricing
  • Design-first concept means facilities breadth is narrower than full-service resorts
  • City dining requires Grab — same Non Nuoc distance from Da Nang as all southern resorts

Who Should Stay Here

Design-conscious travellers, architects, honeymooners who want something distinctive over something polished, and anyone who will appreciate architecture as an active part of the holiday experience. Not the call for families wanting resort amenities or guests who prioritise brand loyalty programmes.
